conflicts.quote: **Chosen: all in-window trades + 1 s last quote.**
conflicts.why: I cannot name a mechanism that makes unsampled stock quotes for three names unstorable. Tokio broadcast drops only a lagged sidecar receiver; the recv loop never awaits disk (bounded try_send to a writer task), so SSE cursors stay independent. Writer overflow is a first-class Path-A gap record, not a keep-set change. Stock ev=Q on the existing stocks WS is the feed we already pay for, not OPRA quote files. One-second last-quote was a cost hedge, not a feasibility wall. PM locked the unsampled keep-set unless architecture proved cannot; I did not.
conflicts.proposal: Path-A appends every decoded StreamKind::Trade and every decoded StreamKind::Quote already delivered on StockStreamHub for the locked trio. Recv loop still never awaits I/O; Lagged(n), channel-full, hub Closed/reconnect, and persist fault become gap records. Do not persist LivePrice (it already collapsed trade vs mid).

conflicts.quote: Path-A and Path-B append only while `MarketPhase::classify(now) == Rth` (09:30–16:00 ET, weekdays).
conflicts.why: MarketPhase has no premarket arm: weekday 04:00–09:30 is ClosedPre and after 16:00 is AfterClose. Filtering Path-A on Rth throws Massive ticks the stocks path already received. The same predicate starves PM's inclusive 16:00 Path-B mark because t<=16:00:00 is a millisecond. The warmer interval loop has no phase gate, so an already-paid fetch in [16:00, 16:05) can fill that mark without new REST.
conflicts.proposal: Path-A appends already-received stocks-path events for locked names on eligible ET weekdays, including ClosedPre/AfterClose events that arrive; weekend stays ineligible. Path-B persists at most one already-paid snapshot per clock-aligned ET mark in 09:30, 09:35, …, 16:00; the 16:00 mark may be filled by the first already-paid fetch with ET time in [16:00, 16:05). Completeness is claimed only against RTH 09:30–16:00.

conflicts.quote: Persist interval **300 s** wall-clock per symbol, **independent of** `WARM_INTERVAL_SECS`.
conflicts.why: Elapsed 300s from first persist is not PM's clock-aligned grid. A mid-session start at 11:07 would write 11:07, 11:12, … and could not be audited as 09:30/09:35/…/16:00. Independence from WARM_INTERVAL_SECS still stands: the ~25s warmer firehose is not the Path-B series.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the persist hook only inside refresh_analytics after a successful compute (no new REST, still no spawn_capture). On each already-paid success for a locked name, assign floor(now_et, 5min); persist at most one snapshot per mark in 09:30–16:00 inclusive; a missing mark is an honest Path-B gap. Watchlist, mark, and interval predicates run before keeping vendor.

conflicts.quote: UX will carry **distinct literals** through the UI for `not_due` / `not_storing` / `missing` / `empty_attempted` / `gap` / `unreadable` / `recording` / `closed`, independently for price tape vs structure snapshots, and will not render a tape occupant as a “present live session book.”
conflicts.why: UX bans coverage cells present/missing on this vehicle; my missing collides. not_due collapses ineligible-weekend, not-expected-pre-store, and before-RTH. closed collapses PM's partial vs complete RTH (AC-19, AC-34). One gap token conflates Path-A hub/writer lag with a missing Path-B 5-minute mark. Copy is UX-owned; I should not have pushed coverage-colliding tokens as literals.
conflicts.proposal: Type-level occupancy, independently per path, includes at least: ineligible_weekend, not_expected_pre_store, not_storing, no_identity, empty_while_storing, path_a_hub_gap, path_b_mark_gap, unreadable, partial, complete_rth. complete_rth means capture-on covered 09:30–16:00 ET (Path-B marks are snapshot or honest gap; Path-A may be empty). None convert to MarketDataSourceKind::LiveMassive or coverage present. UX maps these to closed literals; I do not author the strings.

conflicts.quote: Hard cap **8** names at config parse; production refuse if empty or over cap.
conflicts.why: PM locked a non-editable trio this slice. Cap-8 is an operator-editable watchlist (Out) and is the hub max_sessions coupling I flagged. Default three names are already a subset of DEFAULT_LIQUID; v1 must not grow hub membership.
conflicts.proposal: Sibling closed set (not an alias of ENSURE_SYMBOLS, WARM_SYMBOLS, or universe) whose v1 members are exactly SPY, QQQ, IWM. Ensure-set edits still must not resize the tape. Expansion remains Future plus owner.

conflicts.quote: PM will accept production **fail-closed** on a dedicated tape body root when tape is enabled (default on), including conflict with ring and session-archive roots.
conflicts.why: Default-on plus construct-refuse on a missing root takes down serve, which is a desk outage. That contradicts best-effort-isolated-or-null and PM AC-23 (store not configured, trader desk remains available). production-fails-closed still applies to an explicitly enabled store and to root identity conflicts (tape must not share the session-archive or ring body root).
conflicts.proposal: Default unset/disabled yields not_storing and the listener still binds. Explicit enable refuses construct if the dedicated tape root is missing, unwritable, or conflicts with ring / session-archive index / session-archive body root. No nested default path. Runtime write failure still swallows and leaves bundle, scan, SSE, and ensure intact.

conflicts.quote: `78% of the day captured` as a headline is a renamed count with a completeness connotation the data does not carry unless PM locks a session window **and** both paths report against it (they have not, in this BRIEF).
conflicts.why: PM R1 locked RTH 09:30–16:00 as the completeness clock and requires partial ≠ complete RTH as distinguishable operator outcomes (AC-19, AC-34). Occupancy must carry capture-on coverage so those classes are observable. Percent headlines and verified-complete copy stay banned. The claim that no session window was locked is stale given R1-pm.
conflicts.proposal: Derive partial vs complete_rth from recorded capture-on interval versus 09:30–16:00 ET, independent of tick counts. List/load still prints Path-A kind counts and Path-B snapshot counts. UX adds closed literals for those two classes; never a percent and never coverage present/missing.

conflicts.quote: I am **not** sampling Path-A to dodge volume; if the already-received stocks stream cannot be appended for three names, that is an R2 architecture conflict, not a quiet “trades only” narrowing.
conflicts.why: Architect showed unsampled quotes on these names can run at hundreds to thousands per second — enough to put the live tick path at risk and to approach quote-file volume this BRIEF culled. Trades-only would drop the mid the desk anchors on. I cannot defend an unsampled-all-quotes lock, and I will not fall back to trades-only.
conflicts.proposal: Path-A keep-set this slice is every in-window last-trade print plus the last quote per 1-second bucket (vendor clock when present, else an explicit receive-clock — quality not collapsed). Both kinds remain on the tape and in operator counts. Trades-only stays rejected. Denser quotes are Future.

conflicts.quote: Extended-hours stock events that already arrive **are kept** (do not throw paid ticks) but are **not required** to call a day complete.
conflicts.why: The BRIEF job is an open-to-close day. Architect appends only during regular hours; premarket and afterhours are out of window, not empty. Keeping extended-hours ticks is a volume and occupancy expansion I added beyond open-to-close.
conflicts.proposal: Capture window is regular hours 09:30–16:00 America/New_York on ET weekdays. Out-of-window ticks are not stored and are not empty-while-storing. Premarket/afterhours tape stays Future.

conflicts.quote: That identity may be claimed **complete RTH** only if Path-A was storing across that window **and** every 5-minute mark either has a snapshot or is an honest **gap** (not silently filled).
conflicts.why: A through-window day with Path-B all gaps, or Path-A zero prints, would still pass this test and be labeled complete. That is a fabricated open-to-close success. UX correctly forbids a completeness headline and forbids treating a quiet Path-A day as a failed capture.
conflicts.proposal: Drop operator-facing “complete RTH” as a success class. Keep partial (capture started after 09:30 or stopped before 16:00) distinct from a through-window day. Empty-while-storing, Path-B gaps, and kind/snapshot counts remain the honesty surface. No percent completeness.

conflicts.quote: Persist interval **300 s** wall-clock per symbol, **independent of** `WARM_INTERVAL_SECS`.
conflicts.why: Elapsed 300 s from first in-window persist is not the same series as clock-aligned 09:30, 09:35, …, 16:00. Marks would drift with process start and warmer jitter, so “at most one per 5-minute mark” and “this mark is a gap” are not observable, and Tuesday 09:35 cannot be compared to Wednesday 09:35.
conflicts.proposal: Keep Path-B on the already-paid warm/refresh persist hook, first in-window persist immediate, no extra vendor fetch. At most one snapshot per America/New_York 5-minute mark from 09:30 through 16:00 inclusive. Wall-clock 300 s is not a substitute for those marks.

conflicts.quote: At least: `not_due` (weekend / future / before RTH), `not_storing` (store disabled), `missing` (due weekday, no identity), `empty_attempted` (window open, zero records), `gap` (lag/disconnect/drop recorded), `unreadable` (index without loadable body), `recording` (RTH open), `closed` (post-16:00 ET with whatever was written).
conflicts.why: `missing` and `not_due` on the tape vehicle are coverage words (`missing`, `not yet due`). Printing them as tape occupancy lets a tape miss read as a session-archive hole, which present-is-live-paid-only and UX’s hard ban forbid. A single `closed` after 16:00 also hides partial vs empty-while-storing vs gap, which must stay separate outcomes.
conflicts.proposal: Keep Path-A and Path-B occupancy independent in the store. Operator literals follow UX’s closed tape set, plus a tape-specific ineligible/not-due word that is not coverage `not yet due`, plus a gap literal that is not `no path-a ticks`. Never print `missing` or `present` on tape. After 16:00 the operator can still tell partial from empty from gapped.

conflicts.quote: when tape is enabled, production `construct` refuses if the tape body root is missing, unwritable, or conflicts with ring / session-archive index / session-archive body root (extend `body_root_conflicts`).
conflicts.why: If tape is enabled by default, refusing to start the process because a research tape root is missing or unwritable takes the trader desk down for insurance. Desk-wins isolation requires that case to be not-storing while bundle, scan, live stream, and session-ensure still serve. Colliding with session-archive or ring roots is a different fault: that would overwrite those stores.
conflicts.proposal: Missing or unwritable dedicated tape root → desk still serves, operator outcome is not-storing, no false stored success. Tape root that would collide with session-archive or ring roots may refuse to start. Default-on tape only with a valid dedicated root; otherwise honest not-storing.

conflicts.quote: Persist the **last quote per symbol per 1-second bucket** keyed on vendor `ts_ns` when `ts_ns > 0`, else receive wall-clock with an explicit **receive-clock** basis (timestamp quality is not collapsed).
conflicts.why: Operator Path-A copy cannot print `{n_quote} quotes` or “the quote/mid updates that already arrived” for a last-per-1s sample — that renames a downsample as the stocks-path quote stream (PM AC-3 / S1). A vouched `quote` count would still be a count of stored samples, not of every quote the live desk received.
conflicts.proposal: R2 picks one keep-set. If every already-received stocks-path quote is stored, Path-A print stays kind-split `trade`/`quote` counts. If last quote per 1-second bucket is stored, operator copy must say that and must not claim every arrived quote/mid.

conflicts.quote: Path-A and Path-B append only while `MarketPhase::classify(now) == Rth` (09:30–16:00 ET, weekdays).
conflicts.why: PM keeps extended-hours stock events that already arrive and claims completeness only against RTH. If Path-A drops premarket/afterhours, operator copy cannot say every last-trade/quote the live desk already received; dropped prints would read as if they never happened.
conflicts.proposal: Append Path-A for already-received extended-hours ticks as PM locked; complete-RTH / partial copy stays 09:30–16:00 ET only. If append stays RTH-only, the operator surface needs an out-of-window class — not `no path-a ticks`.

conflicts.quote: Persist interval **300 s** wall-clock per symbol, **independent of** `WARM_INTERVAL_SECS`.
conflicts.why: Standing block and Path-B section print the locked interval. PM’s operator-visible series is clock-aligned 09:30, 09:35, …, 16:00. Elapsed 300 s from first in-window warmer success is a different series; printing clock-aligned 5-minute marks for an elapsed-from-first store is a renamed cadence.
conflicts.proposal: Persist Path-B on the ET clock-aligned 5-minute marks PM locked (at most one per mark, already-paid only). If elapsed-300s is the store, print that (first snapshot as-of, then 300 s) and do not print 09:30/09:35 marks as if they were stored.

conflicts.quote: UX will carry **distinct literals** through the UI for `not_due` / `not_storing` / `missing` / `empty_attempted` / `gap` / `unreadable` / `recording` / `closed`, independently for price tape vs structure snapshots, and will not render a tape occupant as a “present live session book.”
conflicts.why: Coverage already uses `missing`/`present` for live-paid session books. Printing `missing` as a tape cell is this feature’s defining integrity failure. Collapsing weekend, future, and before-RTH into `not_due` also violates `absent-is-not-none` against PM’s ineligible-weekend vs not-expected-pre-store vs partial.
conflicts.proposal: Operator literals stay tape-specific: `no session day tape…` / `no path-a ticks…` / `no path-b snapshots…` / `session day tape not storing` / `session day tape unreadable:` / `not in tape watchlist:` plus PM’s ineligible-weekend, not-expected-pre-store, partial, complete RTH, Path-B gap, Path-B not-capturing, unauthorized. Never coverage `missing` or `present` on this vehicle. Internal enums may differ; list/load copy must not emit those coverage words.

conflicts.quote: Wrapper: tape occupancy = `TapeCapture`; inner “how we fetched” may record live REST as a historical fact.
conflicts.why: Operator load will read whatever the human print shows. Inner `to_wire` / `serialize_capture` bytes stamped `LiveMassive` would label a tape occupant with the session-book provenance token, which copy hard-bans and `present-is-live-paid-only` forbids.
conflicts.proposal: Occupancy and operator print provenance is research tape / never `live_massive`. If an inner fetch fact is shown, it is already-paid REST as history — not `MarketDataSourceKind::LiveMassive` and not coverage `present`.

conflicts.quote: Hard cap **8** names at config parse; production refuse if empty or over cap.
conflicts.why: Standing block prints the locked watchlist this run used. PM AC-5: a name that is not SPY, QQQ, or IWM receives no tape. A cap-8 operator-expanded set would print extra names as in-watchlist while PM forbids an operator-editable set this slice.
conflicts.proposal: Locked-watchlist copy and `not in tape watchlist:` follow PM’s closed trio SPY, QQQ, IWM this slice. Expansion stays Future/owner.

conflicts.quote: `78% of the day captured` as a headline is a renamed count with a completeness connotation the data does not carry unless PM locks a session window **and** both paths report against it (they have not, in this BRIEF).
conflicts.why: PM locked completeness against RTH 09:30–16:00 ET and distinguishable complete RTH vs partial (AC-19, AC-34). The “they have not” clause is false. Percent headlines stay banned; named complete-RTH vs partial classes do not.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the ban on bare percent / “78% of Tuesday”. Add operator-visible complete RTH vs partial. Do not call Path-A-only or Path-B-only a complete day.

conflicts.quote: **PM** accepts the six tape absences (no-ticks / no-snapshots / no-identity / not-storing / unreadable / not-in-watchlist) plus foreign coverage-missing as product states required by `[absent-is-not-none]`, not as UX gold-plating — including that zero Path-A ticks is **not** a `[FAIL]` coverage hole.
conflicts.why: PM S4/AC-34 also requires distinguishable Path-B-gap, partial, ineligible-weekend, not-expected-pre-store, unauthorized, and complete RTH. Collapsing those into the six literals — or using `no path-b snapshots` for both fetch-off and a missing 5-minute mark — is the absence-collapse this lane was designing against.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the six literals as a subset. Extend the closed operator set with PM’s extra classes: Path-B not-capturing ≠ Path-B gap ≠ Path-B empty-while-storing; weekend ≠ not-expected ≠ no-identity; partial ≠ complete RTH. Zero Path-A ticks stays not a coverage `[FAIL]`.

conflicts.quote: **`review` owns** absence of trader UI (AC-27), no S3 ingest (AC-37), and non-absorption of lab UI / body-move / watchlist expansion (AC-38).
conflicts.why: Absence of a trader route/nav/screen is negative space that can silently regress. Risk-based verify marks that `test` (UX AC-U1/U31). Marking AC-27 `review` lets a helpful widget land without a rejecting GATE Q path.
conflicts.proposal: Verify-by for no trader-facing route, nav item, or screen is `test`. Leave `review` on AC-37 (no S3 ingest), AC-38 (no lab UI / body-move / watchlist expansion), standing-block prose, glossary, and SPEC §4 `NO_UI_CHANGE`.

UX: What exact closed literals should list/load print for ineligible-weekend, not-expected-pre-store, partial, and complete-RTH, given coverage present/missing and percent completeness are banned?
UX: Should Path-A hub/writer gap records appear as a first-class list/load absence class, or only as the S2 skip/log line?

Architect: can the same already-paid warm/refresh persist hook key at-most-one Path-B snapshot per ET 5-minute mark (09:30–16:00 inclusive), with first in-window persist still immediate for the current mark, or is elapsed 300 s wall-clock a hard constraint?
Architect: is 16:00 ET inclusive in-window for the close Path-B snapshot, or does phase classification already treat 16:00 as afterhours?
Architect: does v1 config refuse any watchlist other than the locked trio SPY, QQQ, IWM, so a cap-8 expansion cannot silently become the product and cannot occupy extra hub slots?

UX: what closed operator literals should the operator see for (a) a Path-A hub-lag / persist-drop gap, (b) a Path-B 5-minute mark with no snapshot while storing, (c) Path-B not attempted because the already-paid warm fetch is off — each distinct from `no path-a ticks`, `no path-b snapshots`, and `session day tape unreadable`?

Architect: if last-quote-per-1s is stored, does list/load vouch a Path-A `quote` count, and is the 1-second bucket basis (vendor `ts_ns` vs receive-clock) a field the operator print can name so copy does not say every quote that arrived?

Architect: what per-path occupancy tokens will list/load return for empty_attempted, gap (hub lag vs persist skip vs missing 5-minute mark), not_attempted (tape ⊄ warm), recording, closed, and not_due — without using coverage `missing` or `present`?
PM: if R2 accepts last-quote-per-1s, what exact operator phrase replaces “the quote/mid updates that already arrived on that same stocks path”?

PM: exact operator-visible words for complete RTH, partial, Path-B not-capturing, Path-B gap, and not-expected-pre-store, so those classes are not collapsed into `no path-a ticks` / `no path-b snapshots`.
